newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian kids ask Santa for end to guerrilla war.
newsitem.headline: Colombian kids ask Santa for end to guerrilla war.

text.p: One-third of all Colombian children will be asking Santa Claus for an end to the country's long-running guerrilla war this Christmas, according to a survey released on Friday.

But the youngsters are unlikely to find the longed-for gift under the Christmas tree this year. Leftist rebels launched one of their bloodiest offensives in decades in August, sparking an equally violent response from right-wing paramilitary groups and the military.
Hundreds have died in political violence in just those last five months -- so many that government officials have lost count, a spokesman at the presidential press office said.

"Girls and boys will be asking for an end to the guerrilla problem this Christmas. Little ones are most worried by the guerrilla and when they grow up they become more worried about poverty and insecurity," said the survey, conducted by the Fundacion Rafael Pombo and Swedish-based Radda Barnen children's organisations.
A quarter of the 600 children between 8 and 17 said they also would be asking for an end to poverty this Christmas.

One-fifth said they would be asking Santa Claus for more public security to allow them to walk safely through the streets of the five main cities where the poll was carried out. One of those cities, Medellin, Colombia's third largest, is claimed to be the homicide capital of the world.
The survey's margin of error was given as 4 percent.
